CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain sustained during a skiing accident last Saturday (5 days ago). She was skiing double black diamond slopes when she lost control, flipped down the slope, and jammed her index finger on an unknown object. She denies other injuries from the fall. She has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. Pain is rated 7/10. She has not applied ice or worn a splint prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies other injuries from the skiing accident.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation.
Appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, as needed).

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient participates in skiing.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right hand examination: Palpation of the right index finger elicits pain with direct pressure, traction, and squeezing over the distal interphalangeal joint and mid-joint. X-ray of right hand shows normal alignment of all joints and bones with no fractures identified.

RESULTS
Right hand x-ray: Normal, no fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Plan: Apply splint to right index finger. Prescribe Mobic 15 mg once daily (14 tablets). Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine if hand therapy is needed.
